chunks: He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn reported to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil reported to me, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from 'Asim ibn Hamid, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Indeed, the good deed quickest in reward is benevolence, and the evil deed quickest in punishment is tyranny. It suffices as a fault for a person that he looks at faults in others while being blind to the same in himself, or that he reproaches people for what he himself cannot abandon, and that he harms his companion in matters that do not concern him.

key_terms.البر: Birr - benevolence, righteousness, good conduct toward others
key_terms.عيب: Fault, blemish, defect in one's character

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about benevolence, tyranny, and finding fault in others?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), transmitted through Imam al-Baqir (AS) and his forefathers, delivered three interconnected teachings on personal accountability. Spoken in the context of advising the Muslim community, the Prophet warned that benevolence (birr) is the fastest good deed to earn reward, while tyranny (baghy) is the fastest evil to earn punishment. He then identified three character flaws: seeing others' faults while ignoring one's own, criticizing others for sins one commits oneself, and meddling in affairs that do not concern oneself.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 1. He said: ’Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn reported to me from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil, who reported from ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa’dabadi, from Ahmed ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Hamid, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, peace be upon him, reported from his forefathers that: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said:

"Benevolence is a good turn, earning the quickest reward, and tyranny is an evil, earning quickest requital. Enough for ones blemish that one should see faults in others while condoning the same faults in oneself; or scoff at the others for an act from which he himself cannot abstain, and hurt ones companion in matters with which one has no concern."
